category_title: Struggling readers who identify and reject inaccurate speech-to-text transcriptions
student_description: Maggie is a first-grade student who struggles with reading but possesses strong graphosemantic awareness, allowing her to easily spot when speech recognition (SR) software misinterprets her dictation. She is highly motivated to write but becomes frustrated and stalled by inaccurate transcriptions, often skipping the brainstorming phase entirely. She uniquely requires adult dictation to bypass technological failures and metacognitive dialogue to bridge the gap between her oral intent and the written output.

criteria.rationale: Over time, Maggie needs to learn how to independently evaluate graphophonemic representations when technology fails.
criteria.check: The tutor's long-term plan includes thinking aloud to demonstrate the mental process of identifying and evaluating why a transcription is incorrect.

criteria.rationale: Because Maggie tends to skip brainstorming and dictate final compositions directly, she needs sustained modeling of the pre-writing and drafting phases.
criteria.check: The tutor's long-term plan includes explicitly modeling how to brainstorm ideas aloud and use a mix of technology and invented spelling to create drafts.
